value.question: Using the locally indexed NASA Systems Engineering Handbook, compare product verification and product validation: what does each one demonstrate?

steps.description: Search for official primary documentation, release notes, or specifications, then fetch the relevant pages.
Search the locally indexed NASA Systems Engineering Handbook for definitions of product verification and product validation, and extract what each process demonstrates.

key_findings: Product Verification proves that an end product conforms to its requirements or specifications; it answers the question 'Was the end product realized right?' (nasa_Systems_handbook.pdf#p98-chunk-373; nasa_Systems_handbook.pdf#p98-chunk-374).

Product Validation demonstrates that the end product satisfies stakeholder (customer and other interested party) expectations within the intended operational environments; it answers the question 'Was the right end product realized?' (nasa_Systems_handbook.pdf#p98-chunk-374; nasa_Systems_handbook.pdf#p99-chunk-375).

Verification provides objective evidence that every 'shall' statement in the requirements document or specification was met, whereas validation ensures the system functions in the expected manner when placed in the intended environment (nasa_Systems_handbook.pdf#p20-chunk-64; nasa_Systems_handbook.pdf#p99-chunk-375).

Verification testing relates back to the approved requirements set and configuration baseline, while validation relates back to the ConOps document and is conducted under realistic (or simulated) conditions on end products for determining effectiveness and suitability for use in mission operations by typical users (fetch-44b9669f9d11; nasa_Systems_handbook.pdf#p99-chunk-375).
gaps: The evidence does not fully elaborate on the specific methods, inputs, and outputs of the Product Validation Process beyond stating that it is performed by examining products at every level of the product structure against stakeholder expectations (fetch-c6e8049705cd).

The evidence does not specify in detail the full set of distinctions between the processes' activities, such as timing, cost, and schedule implications, beyond noting that verification is conducted first and validation second (fetch-c6e8049705cd; fetch-2410816aaf7a).

The evidence does not quantify the cost-effectiveness of combined verification/validation testing, only noting that expense can be mitigated by combining tests when cost effective and warranted by analysis (nasa_Systems_handbook.pdf#p98-chunk-374).

value.text: Per the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook, product verification demonstrates that an end product conforms to its requirements or specifications, providing objective evidence that every "shall" statement was met, and answers "Was the end product realized right?" Product validation demonstrates that the end product satisfies stakeholder expectations within intended operational environments, answering "Was the right end product realized?" Verification relates back to the approved requirements set and configuration baseline, while validation relates back to the ConOps document and is conducted under realistic or simulated conditions on end products.
